findings.title: GitHub CLI installer executes an unverified moving release
findings.where: .github/actions/ensure-gh/action.yml:26-33 resolves `releases/latest` and streams the selected archive directly into `tar` without a pinned version, digest, or signature check.
findings.what: A compromised upstream release, API response, or release asset can place attacker-controlled executables on PATH for subsequent workflow steps. The same workflow source can also install different binaries on different runs, defeating reproducible supply-chain review.
findings.fix: Pin an explicitly reviewed gh version and expected SHA-256 digest, download the archive to a file, verify it with `sha256sum -c`, and only then extract it.
findings.acceptance: A clean-run test shows the action downloads one fixed version, rejects an archive whose bytes do not match the committed digest, and never extracts before verification.
findings.verifyNote: Re-read lines 18-35 at detached HEAD c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. The preinstalled-gh fast path does not protect runners where gh is absent; that path deterministically fetches `latest` and pipes the archive to tar with no integrity verification.

findings.title: Security-sensitive workflows execute actions through mutable tags
findings.where: The workflows use `actions/github-script@v7`, `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`, `actions/checkout@v6`, `actions/setup-node@v6`, and `actions/upload-artifact@v7` rather than immutable commit SHAs.
findings.what: Owners of those action tags, or an attacker who compromises an upstream action, can retarget a tag and execute changed code with the workflows' tokens and secrets. The cross-review workflow is especially exposed because the Claude action receives `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and a write-capable GitHub token.
findings.fix: Replace every external `uses:` tag with a reviewed full commit SHA, retaining the release tag only in an adjacent update comment; update SHAs through a controlled dependency-update process.
findings.acceptance: A static check over these three workflow files rejects every external `uses:` value that is not pinned to a 40-character commit SHA; workflow tests still pass with the selected SHAs.
findings.verifyNote: Re-read every cited `uses:` line at detached HEAD c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba and confirmed each external reference is a mutable major-version tag. The repository-local ensure-gh reference was not treated as an external tag.

findings.title: Author-vendor detector silently truncates PR commit evidence
findings.where: .github/workflows/agent-cross-review.yml:72-84 requests `pulls.listCommits` once with `per_page: 100` and classifies the joined result without pagination or a truncation guard.
findings.what: For a PR with more than 100 commits, qualifying co-author trailers after the first page are ignored. A mixed-vendor PR can therefore be classified as exclusively Claude or Codex instead of ambiguous, causing the wrong automated reviewer to run despite the workflow's stated evidence rule.
findings.fix: Use `github.paginate(github.rest.pulls.listCommits, ...)` to inspect all returned commits, or explicitly classify any PR whose complete evidence cannot be obtained as ambiguous.
findings.acceptance: A fixture or mocked API test with more than 100 commits and the only opposite-vendor trailer after commit 100 produces `ambiguous`; single-vendor trailers on later pages still produce the correct vendor.
findings.verifyNote: Re-read lines 67-85 at detached HEAD c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. The call has `per_page: 100`, no page parameter, no `github.paginate`, and no total-count/truncation check, while classification immediately consumes that single response.
